diagnostics.message:
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_eks_node_group.this` only orders against `module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_iam_role.this` (through `node_role_arn`); it has no dependency on `module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this`. The node role ARN exists before the AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy / AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly / CNI policies are attached to it, so Terraform may create the node group (and EKS start launching and joining instances) while the role is still permissionless, and on destroy the role can be stripped of permissions before EKS has finished terminating instances and ENIs. The AWS provider documentation for `aws_eks_node_group` explicitly recommends depending on the role policy attachments for exactly this reason. The launch template's own `depends_on` only covers the case where this module creates the launch template.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The EKS managed node group (aws_eks_node_group.this) only references the bare IAM role (node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.this[0].arn) and has no dependency on the role's policy attachments. Per the official aws_eks_node_group docs, the node group must be created after (and destroyed before) its AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy / AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly / CNI policy attachments exist, or nodes fail to register and EKS cannot cleanly delete instances and ENIs. No attribute reference or depends_on expresses this ordering.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_eks_fargate_profile.this` references the pod execution role only through `pod_execution_role_arn` (a dependency on `module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_iam_role.this`), and never depends on `module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this`. The Fargate profile is submitted to EKS with that role before `AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy` and the CNI policy are attached to it, so profile creation can fail (the role is not yet authorized to run Fargate pods / manage ENIs) or pods scheduled to the profile cannot pull images or register. On destroy the reverse ordering is also unguarded. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this]` to `aws_eks_fargate_profile.this`; there is no attribute reference that can carry this ordering, since the attachment exposes no attributes the profile consumes.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_eks_fargate_profile.this only references the pod-execution IAM role (aws_iam_role.this[0].arn) and never the policy attachment. Unlike the node-group modules (which enforce this ordering through a launch template that carries depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this]), the Fargate module has no such path, so the profile can be created before the pod-execution role has AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy attached. IAM is eventually consistent, so Fargate pods scheduled right after will fail with authorization errors until the policy propagates. The profile should depend_on module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this (a bare depends_on is required — no attribute on the profile can reference the attachment to infer it implicitly).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The Fargate profile (aws_eks_fargate_profile.this) references only the bare pod-execution IAM role (pod_execution_role_arn) and — unlike the node-group modules, which have no launch template to transitively depend on the attachments — has no dependency at all on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this. The pod execution role needs AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy / CNI policy attached before Fargate pods can run, so the profile should be ordered after the attachments; nothing in the configuration expresses this.
